general.reason: The paper states '38 of the 39 tasks are learned to INST at every degree and every seed' but then contradicts this two paragraphs later: 'of the 190 solved cells per initialisation (38 tasks × 5 degrees), 186 are INST under random-phase initialisation and 177 under roots-of-unity initialisation.' If only 186/190 cells are INST under random-phase init and 177/190 under roots-of-unity init, then not all tasks are learned to INST at every degree and every seed, making the blanket claim internally inconsistent.

evidence.claim: Section 4.5 presents an internal contradiction about whether instant success (INST) is achieved at every degree and every seed in the learned-encoding ablation, overstating the 'gapless' outcome by ~7% and ~2%.
evidence.excerpt: Section 4.5 states: "38 of the 39 tasks are learned to INST at every degree and every seed..." Two paragraphs later, the same section reports "of the 190 solved cells per initialisation (38 tasks × 5 degrees), 186 are INST under random-phase initialisation and 177 under roots-of-unity initialisation"... These statements cannot both be true: if some cells are GROK/GROKT, then not all cells reach INST.

judge_panel.reason: The paper states '38 of the 39 tasks are learned to INST at every degree and every seed' but then contradicts this two paragraphs later: 'of the 190 solved cells per initialisation (38 tasks × 5 degrees), 186 are INST under random-phase initialisation and 177 under roots-of-unity initialisation.' If only 186/190 cells are INST under random-phase init and 177/190 under roots-of-unity init, then not all tasks are learned to INST at every degree and every seed, making the blanket claim internally inconsistent.

Section 4.5 first states, "Under both initialisations, 38 of the 39 tasks are learned to INST at every degree and every seed," but later in the same section says "of the 190 solved cells per initialisation ... 186 are INST under random-phase initialisation and 177 under roots-of-unity initialisation" and that "A small minority of cells do exhibit a short grokking-style gap." Those statements are inconsistent about whether all successful learned-encoding runs/cells are INST.

The paper does indeed contain this contradiction; it claims on page 11 that '38 of the 39 tasks are learned to INST at every degree and every seed' but subsequently states that 'of the 190 solved cells per initialisation (38 tasks × 5 degrees), 186 are INST under random-phase initialisation and 177 under roots-of-unity initialisation', making the first statement factually inconsistent with the second.
